in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your situation, I need to ask you some questions.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have a son, Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions.

Since Alex is 17, I need to know: Is Alex currently in approved education or training? (For example, is he in school, college, doing A-levels, or an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not in school or college anymore - he left that. But he has started an apprenticeship, actually. He's doing a training course in Wales.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify one important detail about Alex's apprenticeship.

Is Alex's apprenticeship specifically an **apprenticeship in England**, or is it an apprenticeship/training programme in Wales?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's an apprenticeship in Wales, not England. He's doing his training there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

First, do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. And finally, is Alex working 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work that many hours - the apprenticeship keeps him busy but it's not like a full-time job on top of that. And no, he doesn't get any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Based on the information you've provided, **you should be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- Alex is 17 and lives at home with you in the UK
- Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they remain in approved education or training
- Importantly, the rules state that Child Benefit **stops** if a child "starts an apprenticeship **in England**"
- Since Alex's apprenticeship is in **Wales** (not England), this specific exclusion doesn't apply to him
- Alex is not working 24+ hours per week and is not claiming benefits in his own right

Therefore, Alex's apprenticeship in Wales should count as approved training, and you remain eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If you're already receiving it, you should be able to continue receiving it for Alex.
